{
    name: "date-off-by-one",
    symptom: "The days left until a due date are counted from the current time instead of from the start of the day, so after midday a to-do due tomorrow says it is due today, and one due today says it is overdue.",
    file: "src/server/dates.ts",
    trigger: "POST /api/todos with a dueOn of tomorrow, after 12:00 UTC",
  },
  ...

apps/sample/src/server/app.ts:56:  const present = (row: TodoRow): Todo => ({ ...row, daysLeft: row.dueOn ? daysUntil(row.dueOn, now(), bugs) : null });
apps/sample/src/web/invariants.ts:9:  const expected = daysUntil(dueOn, now);

The incident was reported by the browser: the server said daysLeft 0 for a to-do due 2026-11-17 at 20:21 UTC on the 16th, and the calendar says 1. flags.ts points at dates.ts: with date-off-by-one on, daysUntil rounds the distance from the current instant instead of from the start of today, so three hours and forty minutes before midnight rounds down to zero. The only caller is present() in app.ts, which passes the app's flags. The reproduction builds the app with the flag on and the clock fixed at the incident's time, posts a to-do due tomorrow and asserts daysLeft 1; a second test posts one due today and asserts 0, because the same rounding makes today read as overdue.

messages.text: The cause is the branch in daysUntil that measures from now instead of from midnight. The fix deletes that branch, and with it the bugs parameter, which then has no reader: the function counts calendar days for every caller. present() in app.ts stops passing the flags. The flag's entry in flags.ts gets fixedBy: "inc-ec6c6789" so SAMPLE_BUGS=date-off-by-one is still accepted and now changes nothing. The symptom test in api.test.ts steps aside once the entry is marked, and the browser's own check in src/web/invariants.ts keeps calling daysUntil with two arguments, so no test is touched.
